title: Brothers learning his instruments; Henry, Rudy and father's death
summary: Brunies bought instruments that his brothers then picked up and learned; Allen asks about brother Henry, ages of siblings and the father's death at about 62.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah, yeah. Yeah, yeah. You really learned by yourself, and you didn't have any lessons except a couple you learned.

And the reason the other boys learned, I went out and bought the instruments and I couldn't blow them like a trombone. Trombone? They were on the yard or laid on the table. Mm-hmm. Older's brother Henney come along, he picked it up. He learned it. Well, he's dead now.

Well, can you tell us a little bit about your brother, Henry, because he's not here, of course, to talk for us. Well, he was a hot friend. He was a wonderful, I've heard. Yes, he was. He was a showman with his son. I had that to say. How much younger was he than you? He was younger than you? Oh, yeah. Next to him. About five years. About five years. And, uh...

He'd be about 65. What's his name? Merritt and them, they did the same thing. I'd buy an instrument, they'd come along behind me and pick it up and blend it up. That's how they all went out. I'd blow a blow and essence.

How much older was Rudy than you? About... Oh, Rudy was about three or four. About five years. About five years old. Oh, you're 69? He'd be... Yeah, about five. That's right. That's right. I'm right.
